desc: **Task 0 (ideation):** Establish monotone-grid structure, heap approach, duplicate-free expansion rule, and rejected alternatives.

**Task 1 (implementation):** Full solution code — fast I/O, descending sort, truncation to `m=min(N,K)`, heap search with canonical-parent rule, print K-th popped value; localize heap functions/arrays inside `main()`.

**Task 2 (validation):** Logic verified — f = A_iB_j + C_k(A_i+B_j) is increasing in each of A_i,B_j,C_k (all values ≥ 1), so after descending sorts f is non-increasing componentwise; canonical-parent expansion generates each triple exactly once with parent value ≥ child value, so the K-th pop is the K-th largest.

**Task 3 (performance check):** Heap holds ≈K entries (only one mandatory child per pop, extra children only when i==0/j==0); ~5·10⁵ pops and ~5·10⁵+ pushes of 2-tuples with packed index — runs comfortably in time.
**Task 4 (edge cases):** m³ ≥ K always (m=N ⇒ N³≥K; m=K ⇒ K³≥K), so heap never empties; N=1/K=1 handled (no children pushed); ties safe since packed ints break comparisons.
